plain: When the inventor Nikola Tesla died in 1943, the story goes, the FBI, the US federal police, seized his papers, and an engineer named John G. Trump was sent to go through them. Michels tells it again and again on the show, in his own words and without naming a source. He describes Trump as a professor at MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, "the country's leading radar expert at the time, and Donald Trump's uncle." According to Michels, the FBI raided Tesla's apartment by Bryant Park in New York, and the files "were seized and put in a vault." Trump's job was to see whether anything in them "would be of service to national security," or would "confer any tactical warfare advantages to the United States." Michels also says the researcher Bill Moore interviewed Trump for a documentary about the Philadelphia Experiment, a story of a secret wartime Navy experiment. A researcher who goes by RedPandaKoala tells it more simply: Trump was so clever that when Tesla died the government called on him to "go through like all of his notes." One of Michels's tellings dates it loosely to the 1940s instead of 1943. It is told because it would mean Tesla's work was treated as a possible military secret.
